newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ministers to discuss Irish compromise on potato marketing.
newsitem.headline: Ministers to discuss Irish compromise on potato marketing.

text.p: The Farm Council will discuss on Monday a new Irish presidency compromise over a long-standing proposal to establish EU-wide potato marketing rules, an Irish official said.

The Irish document differs from the Commission's proposal of November 1992, COM(185)92, by giving producer groups a greater role in line with that agreed under a recent reform of the fruit and vegetable sector.
Ireland has also suggested setting up an operational fund, jointly financed by producers and the EU. It would not be used to fund withdrawal of market surpluses.
Rules would be set for trade with non-EU countries, a framework for national aids and a monitoring system in line with that approved for fruit and vegetables.

"Around five or six countries support the proposal but others are against a common marketing organisation and prefer national rules," the official said, commenting on discussions this week in the Special Agricultural Committee.
Spain, Greece, Portugal, Italy and Ireland are the main supporters. Opposition comes from northern member states, notably Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark and Belgium.
The Commission's original proposal was for a "lightweight" regime setting common trading standards, promotion of producer groups and rules for trade with non-EU countries.

In December 1995, the Spanish presidency tried unsuccessfuly to break the deadlock between northern and southern states by putting forward a compromise including quality standards and the creation of an operational fund.
But officials were pessimistic of a breakthrough next week.
"There's still a substantail blocking minority," said an official from a northern member state.
